articles.title_orig: ‘GTA 6’ Will Face Something It Couldn’t Have Prepared For At Launch
articles.title_zh: ‘GTA 6’ Will Face Something It Couldn’t Have Prepared For At Launch
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar reportedly plans to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027.
GamesBeat reported the news based on four sources who asked to remain anonymous. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are yet to comment.
If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.
The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”
Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.
Indeed, 12 months ago, Zelnick said the industry was “moving towards PC,” telling CNBC’s Squawk Box that the video game business was trending towards “open rather than closed.”
In 2024, Zelnick was asked if the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 was set in stone . Here’s his response in full:
Assuming GTA 6 does come to PC early next year, one of the big questions players will have is how it runs compared to on consoles. Rockstar has yet to confirm the performance of GTA 6 on consoles, so we're still in the dark when it comes to frames-per-second and resolution. But the expectation is that any PC version would be capable of better performance, assuming your rig is powerful enough.

articles.title_orig: New nonstop Lufthansa flight announced from Columbus to Frankfurt
articles.title_zh: New nonstop Lufthansa flight announced from Columbus to Frankfurt
articles.content_orig:
Published: October 19, 2026
(COLUMBUS) The Columbus Regional Airport Authority, Lufthansa Airlines, JobsOhio and One Columbus today announced that Central Ohio's first nonstop flight to Europe will launch in May 2027, connecting John Glenn Columbus International Airport (CMH) with Frankfurt Airport (FRA) in Germany. The new service marks a major milestone for the Columbus Region and Ohio, providing direct access to one of the world's leading international hubs and creating new opportunities for businesses, travelers and visitors throughout the state.
“Today's announcement is a tremendous milestone for the Columbus Region and Ohio,” said Daren Griffin, CRAA President and CEO. “Lufthansa's new nonstop service to Frankfurt provides our passengers with a direct link to one of the world's strongest global networks, enhancing connectivity, competitiveness and continued growth. We are grateful to Lufthansa, JobsOhio, One Columbus, our business community and so many others whose partnership helped make this opportunity possible. At a time of extraordinary transformation for our airports and our region, this new service establishes Ohio's gateway to continental Europe. It strengthens our state's connections to the global economy and creates new opportunities for communities across Ohio. We couldn't be more excited about what it means for our businesses, travelers and the future of Ohio”
This will be Ohio's first and only nonstop flight to Germany, serving hundreds of daily passengers from Columbus and across Ohio who travel to Europe each day. Lufthansa will operate the service with a Boeing 787 Dreamliner featuring the airline's Allegris cabin experience, including 28 lie-flat business class seats, 28 premium economy seats and 231 economy seats, for a total of 287 seats.
“We are very pleased to connect Columbus and the state of Ohio directly with our Frankfurt hub, the first intercontinental flight from this great city,” said Dirk Janzen, Lufthansa Group Vice President of Passenger Sales, the Americas. “The new service will provide both business and leisure travelers with a convenient nonstop connection to Germany, as well as onward destinations across our Lufthansa Group network. The launch of this route is an important step in our continued expansion in the United States, our most important market outside the Lufthansa Group’s home markets. We look forward to strengthening the connections between Ohio and Europe, and to welcoming travelers from Columbus and the surrounding region,” Janzen added.
The flight will provide unprecedented connectivity for the 38 German-based companies operating in the Columbus Region and further support all German companies investing in Ohio and employing thousands of Ohioans across the state. Through Lufthansa's Frankfurt hub, travelers will have convenient access to more than 130 destinations across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and India.
The new service is also expected to make it easier for international visitors, investors and talent to access the Columbus Region and explore opportunities across Ohio, further supporting the state's economic development efforts.
“Ohio is committed to building a collaborative partnership with Lufthansa to support the success of this new route and strengthen the significant ties that benefit both of our regions,” said Ohio Governor Mike DeWine. “This new route will be transformative, giving our state access to critical markets in Germany, Europe and the world while establishing stronger economic, research, cultural and educational exchanges.”
Germany is the third-largest source of international investment in Ohio, behind only Japan and Canada. More than 750 German-owned business establishments operate in Ohio, second only to Japan, according to the Ohio Department of Development, and German companies support approximately 41,000 jobs across the state, according to the Transatlantic Economy 2025 report. Ohio businesses also exported nearly $1.4 billion in goods to Germany in 2023. Overall, Ohio ranks third in the nation for foreign direct investment, with about 4,000 companies from 42 countries operating in the state.
The new route builds on the success of JobsOhio’s Air Service Restoration program, which works with airports, regional partners and airlines to establish routes that are important to economic development. JobsOhio created the program after businesses and stakeholders said during a 2019 statewide listening tour that air service at Ohio airports had declined more sharply than in competitor states. Through the program, JobsOhio and regional partners share revenue guarantees that reduce the risk for airlines launching new service.
Since 2020, it has helped bring 32 new routes and 15 route expansions with six airlines to five Ohio airports, adding more than 590,000 new seats and more than 187,000 additional seats each year and generating an estimated $230 million in annual economic impact. JobsOhio has committed $36.8 million in revenue guarantees, alongside $10.1 million from local partners.
“Businesses, including the German companies that employ tens of thousands of Ohioans, tell us that better air service is essential to investing and creating jobs in Ohio,” said JobsOhio President and CEO J.P. Nauseef. “We listened, and this direct link to Frankfurt is exactly what our Air Service Restoration program was built to deliver.”
The new air service comes as the Columbus Region experiences some of the strongest economic growth in the country. The Columbus metro leads the Midwest in job creation, adding nearly 12,000 jobs between March 2025 and March 2026, with a growth rate more than 18 times the national average. The Region’s population also grew by more than 21,000 residents in 2025, twice the national growth rate. The new international connection is expected to further strengthen the Region’s ability to attract businesses, investment and talent from around the world.
“The Columbus Region is in the middle of an extraordinary stretch of job creation and business investment, and now we’re adding direct access to one of Europe’s most important business hubs,” said Jonas Peterson, Chief Economic Development Officer and President of One Columbus. “That’s a significant competitive advantage. It makes it easier for global companies to invest here, strengthens connections for businesses already operating in our Region and improves our ability to compete for the next major project. We have tremendous economic momentum right now, and this new connection gives us an opportunity to accelerate it even further.”
The Columbus Region continues to attract global investment and advanced industries, including recent commitments from companies such as Anduril, Intel and Bayer. The new Lufthansa service further strengthens Ohio's position as a destination for business growth and international commerce.
The CMH-FRA route will begin operating in May 2027, with bookings available beginning Tuesday, Oct. 20. Service will operate three times weekly on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. Flights will depart Columbus at 4:20 p.m. and arrive in Frankfurt at 6:15 a.m. (local times).
The Lufthansa Group is a globally operating aviation group, with more than 100,000 employees worldwide. It is Europe's largest airline group by revenue, generating revenue of EUR 39.6 billion (EUR 39,597 million) in the 2025 financial year. The Lufthansa Group comprises mulitple business segments, including Passenger Airlines, Logistics, Technology (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul), as well as other companies and group functions, including IT services and Lufthansa Aviation Training.
The Lufthansa Group’s portfolio of airlines includes Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, ITA Airways, Eurowings and Discover Airlines, connecting customers to destinations around the globe. articles.content_orig:
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a longtime educator and respected member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday morning. Full Story
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a longtime educator and respected member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday morning. Full Story
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a beloved educator and longtime member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday, 8 Cheshvan, 5787.
Rabbi Malov suffered a sudden cardiac arrest shortly after waking up and washing Negel Vasser. Emergency responders were called to his home but were unable to revive him.
His sudden passing has shocked the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad and his many friends and acquaintances throughout Israel and around the world.
Rabbi Malov served as the Rebbe’s Shliach in Kfar HaRif and dedicated much of his life to Jewish education. For many years, he directed the neighborhood’s evening yeshiva program, where hundreds of children gathered nightly in the local shul to study Torah.
Friends described him as a devoted educator and accomplished Torah scholar, knowledgeable in both Nigleh and Chassidus, who worked tirelessly to spread Torah learning.
He also organized annual Kinusei Torah in the neighborhood around Yom Tov, in accordance with the Rebbe’s directive to hold Torah gatherings during the holidays.
Rabbi Malov was the son-in-law of Rabbi Yitzchak Yehuda Yeruslavsky , Rov of Nachlas Har Chabad and a leading Chabad Rov.
He was born in Bnei Brak to Rabbi Tzvi Eliyahu Malov , OBM, a longtime Chabad communal activist in Yerushalayim who passed away approximately six years ago, and Mrs. Chana Chaya Malov , daughter of R’ Yaakov Moshe Hakohen Halperin , who passed away in Tishrei 5751 at the age of 40.
He is survived by his wife, Mrs. Nechama Dina Malov , and their children: Menachem Mendel, Shterna Sarah Kramer, Devorah Leah , and Mushka .
The levaya will depart from his home in Nachlas Har Chabad at 12:30 PM, passing the local Talmud Torah and central shul before proceeding to Shamgar in Yerushalayim.
The levaya will depart Shamgar at 3:00 PM for burial at Har Hamenuchos in Yerushalayim.

Jingle Jangle is about to be sold out in even more stores.
Trader Joe’s — home of infamous seasonal treats like Apple Cider Donuts , Pumpkin-Flavored Joe-Joe’s and the Christmas favorite Jingle Jangle — has announced more locations are on the way.
The nation’s favorite grocery chain recently announced on its website that shoppers will see even more stores — over 30. The new locations will be in the following three cities and will likely open in 2027:
The move comes after the California-based company revealed 25 new spots were coming across 14 states.
Some recent openings include West Palm Beach, Fla., on June 12, the New Orleans, La., location on June 10 and the Tucson, Ariz., location on May 29.
As of Oct. 12, the fan-favorite grocery chain revealed it will open the following:
Trader Joe’s did not set an opening date for the new locations, but it did tell Nexstar that locations marked as “opening soon” typically open three to six months after announcing them online.
The newest spot open to the public is in Reading, MA, as shoppers could start browsing aisles on Oct. 14.
In fact, TJ’s has kept up a fairly steady growth rate, opening 34 stores in 2024 and 43 stores in 2025.
The grocery chain currently has over 600 storefronts, but there are still states without a location, including Alaska, Hawaii, Mississippi, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, West Virginia and Wyoming.

articles.title_orig: Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen government training camp, officials say
articles.title_zh: Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen government training camp, officials say
articles.content_orig:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces
At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.
The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.
There will be an inquiry into how so many troops were left so exposed to a Houthi attack. In mid-September, the group began a fresh push on forces backing the UN-recognised government by pushing south along the Red Sea coast to try to take control of the Bab al-Mandab waterway.
Reliable assessments of the death toll in the fighting over the last month are hard to gather, but it is running into the many thousands. A Saudi airstrike on Sunday killed nine, including five children and two women.
Rashad al-Alimi, the president of the UN-recognised government, said those killed on Monday were new recruits, and he vowed an immediate hard response. He said the incident “affirmed that targeting the recruits reflects the Houthi militias’ approach of resorting to cowardly terrorist attacks whenever they face pressures or their Iranian-backed sabotage plots falter”.
On Monday he phoned the UN secretary general, António Guterres, to ask for the UN to classify the Houthis as a foreign terrorist organisation.
The Shabwa provincial authority said: “Targeting recruits constitutes a military escalation and a blatant assault on the province’s security.” Its governor, Awad bin al-Wazir, visited the wounded in hospitals, and called for extra air defences, saying troops were fighting across six fronts.
The killings underline the dangers of large numbers of troops gathering in one place within reach of the Houthi ballistic missile arsenal. The training camp was struck by three ballistic missiles while the recruits lined up in formation.
Houthi forces have also cut the road between government-run Shabwa and the Houthi-run Bayda governorate.
The Houthi military spokesperson said: “Our armed forces targeted the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations in al-Alam camp, which is run by Saudi officers in the eastern regions. The targeting resulted in the fall of dozens of dead and wounded from the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations, including Saudi officers.
“We warn the deceived ones against responding to the Saudi enemy’s calls to lure them with his defiled money to the pyres of death, and to exploit them instead of his soldiers who are indifferent to their lives.”
A Yemen government spokesperson said the site struck was not a military target linked to the current fighting but “a training centre where new recruits in the internal security forces of Shabwa governorate receive training and qualification programmes.”
They added: “This reveals the criminal nature of this assault, which targeted young people in the preparation and qualification phase to carry out their security duties, far from the frontlines.”
Separately the Houthis claim to have hit the anti-Houthi Giant Brigades of southern Yemen in six strikes in the areas of al-Suqya and Ras al-Ara. Southern forces are said to have been making progress in edging Houthi forces out of control of the area around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrowest waterway taking ships from the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.
Fighting is also under way as Houthis try to mount a siege of Taiz, where citizens have been calling for greater air protection. In the city there seems to be a determination not to capitulate, but conditions are deteriorating as Houthis close access points.
It is not clear whether the Houthis have decided to slow the pace of attacks on Saudi airports and energy installations, or they are running low on munitions.
The Saudi Aramco headquarters was struck last weekend and some airlines have said they will not yet resume using Riyadh airport. The airport reopened at the weekend after being attacked this month .
Egypt’s parliament has postponed a vote on whether to send troops to Saudi Arabia despite extending the debate to a second day as MPs demanded more than two minutes each to speak. The vote is now likely to be held next week.
A two-thirds majority is required, and some opposition parties have signalled their intention to vote against or abstain. Disputes centre on the extent of the mission and whether it will involve sending troops into Yemen to help Saudi Arabia, and whether Egyptian troops inside Saudi Arabia would become targets for Houthi attacks.
The delay also gives the Egyptians time to see if Iran can persuade the Houthis to hold back, and for Saudi Arabia to confirm the renewal of badly needed loans to Egypt.
Egypt has resisted any ground intervention in Yemen, dating back to the 1962-67 war, when Gamal Abdel Nasser sent troops to back the republicans in North Yemen against the Saudi- and British-backed royalists. The incursion was intended to be minimal, but escalated to as many as 70,000 soldiers. Estimates of Egyptians killed range from 10,000-26,000.

articles.title_orig: It’s hard to imagine wireless headphones ever getting lighter than these
articles.title_zh: It’s hard to imagine wireless headphones ever getting lighter than these
articles.content_orig:
The Final Porta weigh just 40 grams and offer up to eight hours of battery life.﻿
The Final Porta weigh just 40 grams and offer up to eight hours of battery life.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
If you’re on the hunt for lightweight wireless headphones but wearing earbuds or clip-ons never feels comfortable or secure, a relatively obscure Japanese headphone maker could have the solution. Final’s new Porta headphones feature an on-ear design supported by a headband but with a structure made from a single piece of wire so they weigh just 40 grams. For comparison, Marshall’s recently-launched Milton A.N.C. are also designed to be smaller on-ear headphones but weigh 200 grams.
The Final Porta are available for preorder now through the company’s online store for 12,800 yen (around $80) with black or orange ear pads and shipping expected to start on October 23rd. The company also has an Amazon shop for US-based customers, but the Porta aren’t listed there yet.
Sporting a design that looks loosely inspired by the lightweight headphones Sony bundled with its Walkmans decades ago, the Porta’s functionality is unsurprisingly basic. A 57mAh battery charges over USB-C and provides up to eight hours of use while the Porta are wirelessly paired to a device using Bluetooth 5.4 and streaming audio over the SBC and AAC codecs. There’s no active noise cancelation which is not uncommon for on-ear headphones that don’t create a full seal, but with an IPX4 rating you should be able to use the Porta in the rain or while working up a sweat without worrying about them getting damaged by the moisture.

articles.title_orig: 10 Mini Gadgets Worth 3D Printing Instead Of Buying
articles.title_zh: 10 Mini Gadgets Worth 3D Printing Instead Of Buying
articles.content_orig:
If you're thinking about buying a 3D printer , you should know that there's no limit to the things that you can make once you get one. While everyone has probably thought about making large pieces, printing smaller items could also result in lots of saved time and money.
For this article, we identified 10 mini gadgets worth 3D printing instead of buying, and we've given some examples for each of them so you can see the benefits. Some of our selections for this roundup include stands and docks for mobile devices, an alternative to keychains, and accessories for tabletop games.
All of the examples that we've included are publicly available from the best sites for free 3D printing projects , though some of them come with the restriction that you can only make them for personal use. They've all been downloaded at least 1,000 times, though, so it's likely the creators have received plenty of feedback and maybe even updated their files as needed to address any concerns raised.
When you buy an Apple Watch , there's no charging stand that comes with it. You'll only get a charging puck, so the smartwatch lies flat on your desk. You can buy a charging stand that holds the watch upright so that you can see the time and notifications, but most options in the market are expensive because they come with extras like wireless charging capabilities or additional space for your iPhone and AirPods. 3D printing this gadget will not only save on costs, but you'll also be able to choose the color that you want.
If you want something simple, there are 3D-printed options like the Apple Watch Charging Stand by Dan_ID on Maker World. With about 59,500 downloads, it holds the smartwatch's charging puck and sets the Apple Watch horizontally with the straps wrapped around it to minimize the space that it occupies on your desk.
Pulsar Designs' Charging Stand for Apple Watch , also available on Maker World and with 13,300 downloads, sets the wearable device vertically instead. This design also holds the charging puck securely, and it's compact while also elevating the smartwatch for a better look at the straps that you chose for the day.
Similar to the Apple Watch charging stand, a phone dock will allow you to see your smartphone's screen at all times, whether it's plugged into its charger or not. These accessories come in all shapes and sizes, but 3D printing one will allow you to choose the exact style that you want depending on how much space you have available on your desk and the size of your phone.
The Phone Stand by GoAftens on Thingiverse is as simple as it gets for this type of accessory. With about 40,100 downloads and originally made for Apple's iPhone 6, it has a hole at the bottom to allow a charging cable to plug into your phone while it's placed vertically on the stand, though you also have the option of setting it horizontally. You can adjust the width of the ledge if you've got a thick phone, such as a foldable, or because your preferred case is bulky.
Moss 3D's Adjustable Phone Stand , which has about 2,500 downloads on Maker World, is a slightly more modern version of the gadget. It's foldable for portability, and you can set it at a variety of angles to suit your needs. It features a locking function to keep it in place even when it's holding a heavier device like a tablet. With its retro aesthetic and your choice of colors for its parts, this phone stand also has more personality than many of the other options in the market.
Toothpaste squeezers are essential for frugal living, and it goes against the principles of the lifestyle if the gadget that you buy costs a lot, breaks easily, or isn't effective. 3D-printed toothpaste squeezers are not only tried and tested, but you'll also be able to make the exact number that you need, in the specific size for your usual toothpaste tubes.
The Toothpaste Squeezer by mgm86, which has been downloaded 28,500 times from Maker World, gives a more precise and direct squeeze than many similar gadgets that have a fixed slot. To use it, you remove the colored cap to insert the toothpaste tube, then re-insert the cap to tighten the grip and further flatten the tube. There are two sizes available for the project, one with a slot length of 58 millimeters and the other at 68 millimeters. You can also customize the colors of the caps depending on the household member who's using each particular brand of toothpaste.
The Ultimate Toothpaste Squeezer by the pro is another option, but it uses rollers to get every drop out of the tube instead of relying on direct pressure from your hands. Downloaded about 20,000 times on Printables, this gadget has a wheel for turning the gears and squeezing the toothpaste tube. It may look complicated, but assembly after 3D printing won't require additional tools, and it can be disassembled for thorough cleaning if necessary.
There are a lot of types of fidget toys you can buy , as they've evolved from just being simple spinners. You can now also click and squeeze them, among many other actions, with the goal of either keeping your mind focused or relieving your stress. If you're still figuring out what kind of fidget toy works the best for you, or if you already know and you want different versions of your favorites, you can 3D print them so that you can customize their size and colors.
Kriswillcode's Mechanical Switch Fidget Click Toy , which has 1,600 downloads on Thingiverse, mimics the feel and sound of typing on a mechanical keyboard. In addition to seven 3D-printed pieces that need to be accurately sized, you'll need a spring like those in retractable pens to assemble this gadget. If done right, you'll get a satisfying click each time you press its button.
For a different kind of fidget toy, there's the Tactile Fidget Rings by GlennovitS 3D. You can get its files from Printables, where it has been downloaded about 42,000 times. This is a print-in-place project, which means there's no assembly necessary after 3D printing, and there are a total of five options for the textures of the rotating rings. There are also four mixed versions that have a different texture for each ring, and of course, you can choose the color that you want when you print them for yourself or to give to your friends and family members.
Open bag clips are very useful in the kitchen, as they help keep food and ingredients fresh by allowing you to reseal the packages. However, when you buy these accessories, they usually come in bundles of different sizes, where some are too big or small, or there are so many that you won't be able to use them all. If you 3D print your open bag clips instead, you're going to get the specific size and quantity that you need, and you can even make them part of a color-coded system in your refrigerator or pantry.
The Crazy Crocodile Clip , made by Newstream and downloaded about 5,700 times on Maker World, is a 3D-printable open bag clip that resembles a crocodile, as its name suggests. It's more than just a fun design, though, as the accessory can keep packages sealed securely. This latest version of the project has a stronger print-in-place hinge for durability than earlier iterations, and as its creator suggested, it can even double as a fidget toy.
Coffee Clip for Open Bags , which has about 24,000 downloads on Printables, adds a resealable cap to the open bag clip for easy pouring of whatever's inside. Pressi, the designer of the 3D-printed gadget, said that it can be used for coffee beans, snacks, spices, and other similar food items in lightweight packages.
If you're always misplacing your keys, a key organizer can help make sure that they're all in one place. Some key organizers are shaped to keep all your keys together for better portability, while others serve as storage for easy access to everyone in the family. When you buy this gadget, you need to check if there's enough space for all your keys, but if you 3D print it, you'll get one with the exact specifications that you need.

articles.title_orig: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.title_zh: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.content_orig:
The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker.
The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker.
A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge . Though Norforge doesn’t name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins.
Concerns over AI-powered cybersecurity breaches have grown as the technology grows more advanced, with hackers using the tools to carry out large-scale attacks. At the same time, rogue AI agents are carrying out attacks of their own after escaping from testing environments.
Researchers at Norforge uncovered the attacks through exposed work on Cairn, an open-source AI platform that describes itself as a “general-purpose problem-solving engine.” With Cairn, users set a start and end point for the AI agents, which document their progress as they move forward with the task. However, as noted by Norforge, hackers can also use the tool to orchestrate cyberattacks using AI agents.
The hacker who broke into more than 100 sites was the “most active” among the exposed Cairn instances discovered by Norforge, waging attacks on companies based in the US, Canada, Australia, and Japan, as reported by Reuters . This attacker laid out “preferred intrusion tactics” using fewer than 100 Chinese characters, with successful breaches taking about 23 hours, according to Reuters . Overall, Nordforge found more than 20 exposed Cairn instances that are “likely malicious.”
In a statement to Reuters , a John Deere spokesperson said there is “no indication that ​sensitive information was accessed” as a result of the attack, while Cummins said it’s “investigating the report of a potential cyber-attack on a website operated by one of our third-party vendors.”
Meanwhile, SharkNinja says the breach impacted a standalone site with product support information, and that it has contained the threat. John Deere, Cumms, and SharkNinja didn’t immediately respond to The Verge ’s request for comment.
Nordforge says it’s working to get the malicious Cairn instances taken down. Cairn’s creator, who goes by @le1xia0, said earlier this month that the platform “was never a ‘hacking tool,’” adding that “misuse is a human decision, not a feature of the engine.”

articles.title_orig: Violent protests multiply across Europe
articles.title_zh: Violent protests multiply across Europe
articles.content_orig:
School conditions, unaffordable housing and the cost of living have brought demonstrators on to the streets in several countries
Europe live – latest updates
Young people have been taking to the streets across Europe, including in Spain, France and Portugal , to protest over their unhappiness at the state of schools and the wider cost of living crisis.
In France, high school pupils have clashed with police in often violent protests over long hours, missing teachers, dilapidated classrooms and an opaque university admissions system. Pupils routinely miss months of teaching due to unfilled staff absences.
Other demonstrators soon joined in, voicing their unhappiness about rising living costs, including over fuel prices after US bombing in effect caused the closure of the strait of Hormuz. The General Confederation of Labour, one of France’s largest unions, has backed the protests and called for lower prices, higher pensions and boosted wages.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron , is nearing the end of his time in the Élysée Palace after serving two terms.
Over the Pyrenees in Spain , activists took to the streets in September over housing prices.
The protests were triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home after an investment fund hiked her rent by 230%. Maricarmen Abascal died a fortnight later after being admitted to hospital.
Protesters have called for rent freezes, halting the evictions of vulnerable people and the regulation of short-term and room rentals.
Similar pleas were made across the Iberian border in Portugal on Saturday, when hundreds gathered in central Lisbon . Portuguese housing prices more than doubled between 2015 and 2024, roughly twice as fast as the EU average, according to official data.
Squeezed household budgets were also at the centre of marches in Milan. Masked rioters seemingly later seized on the protests to throw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and setting fire to barricades made from bar tables. There were also clashes between police and protesters in Turin and Bologna.
Meanwhile, protests in Albania against the prime minister, Edi Rama, entered their seventh day on Monday. Demonstrators have said they are unhappy with perceived corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards.
The education protests in France began in late September, a week after the start of the school year. Protests soon also began springing up in Portugal and Belgium.
In France, demonstrations reached a high point on Saturday as about half a million people turned out to protest against the surging cost of living and join the students demanding better conditions at their schools. That day there were also marches in Belgium, Portugal and Italy.
In Albania, protests have been taking place since the summer, triggered by a luxury coastal development backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
In France, the government has said it will deploy 3,000 more substitute teachers to deal with shortages, and include students in decision-making for schools. It also scrapped plans to increase some university registration fees, which it had announced for next year’s budget.
Fuel protests in mid-September led to an announcement by the Élysée that the government would increase petrol subsidies for certain industries.
Spain’s Socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, attempted to pass emergency housing legislation that included a ban on evictions until 2030 and the regulation of temporary lettings and lettings by room.
The legislation’s defeat at the hands of rightwing and far-right parties in parliament led Sánchez to call a snap election for 29 November, as he told the public he needed a “broader progressive majority” to get new reforms through.
In recent days, the protests have been eclipsed by the violence that played out on the fringes. On Sunday night Macron said it was “unbearable to see our streets ransacked” while, hours later, France’s prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, called for “very limited” and “localised” curfews.
Macron said a distinction must be drawn between what he described as genuine, peaceful demonstrators who were making demands over the cost of living and the education system, and others who “destroy, ransack and loot”.
His interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, appeared to signal the French government was not willing to concede further, as he blamed “far-left” protesters and “criminals who looted and ransacked” buildings across France. The country will go to the polls in April 2027.
Meanwhile, the protests continue. In Paris, about a dozen demonstrators blocked the entrance to the Louvre on Monday, leaving tourists milling outside the world’s most-visited museum.
In Spain, housing campaigners have vowed to keep up the pressure on politicians to address soaring costs, announcing plans for a general strike on 11 November.

articles.title_orig: Nearly 1.6M pounds of meat, poultry products recalled nationwide: FSIS
articles.title_zh: Nearly 1.6M pounds of meat, poultry products recalled nationwide: FSIS
articles.content_orig:
Kayem Foods is recalling more than 1.5 million pounds of hot dogs, bacon, sausage and more meats that may have been stored at unsafe temperatures, U.S. Department of Agriculture regulators announced.
The USDA said ready-to-eat meat and poultry products distributed from the Chelsea, Massachusetts, company "may have experienced temperature abuse during storage."
Kayem said in a statement that it recently discovered a "cooling system malfunction" at one of its warehouses.
"Out of an abundance of caution, we are undertaking this voluntary recall," Kayem Foods President and CEO Matt Monkiewicz said. "We take food safety very seriously and apologize to our valued consumers. Our management team takes full responsibility. We have learned from and corrected the issue and will not allow this to happen again."
So far there have not been any reports of illness linked to the recall. The USDA is concerned that recalled products may be in consumers' refrigerators. Anyone who has a recalled item should throw it away.
Kayem said the affected foods were stored and shipped between June 7, 2026 and Oct. 14, 2026. They were sent to retailers and food service locations nationwide.
The products linked to the recall have establishment numbers "EST. M/P 7839," "EST. P 20935A" and "EST. M 9520" inside the USDA mark of inspection.
The USDA has published a list of the recalled products and their UPC codes.
Among the recalled items are a variety of hot dogs including "Fenway Franks," bologna, kielbasa, bratwurst, beef brisket, bacon, corned beef, ham, al fresco chicken sausage, turkey breast and liverwurst.
Kayem Foods recall by CBS Boston
In 2025, Kayem recalled more than 24,000 pounds of chicken sausage products because they may have been contaminated with pieces of plastic.

articles.title_orig: 4 Cool New Features Your Fitbit Air Is Getting In October 2026
articles.title_zh: 4 Cool New Features Your Fitbit Air Is Getting In October 2026
articles.content_orig:
While the new Fitbit Edge is set to release in late October, the older Fitbit Air remains one of the best affordable fitness trackers you can buy today . It doesn't offer the same experience as a full smartwatch, but the Fitbit Air's comfortable build and versatile set of health and wellness tracking features make it a great alternative to Whoop and other screenless fitness bands.
While the Fitbit Air already comes with most features you'd want from a fitness tracker, Google recently announced several additions and improvements coming alongside the Fitbit Edge later in the month. These include the ability to passively track blood pressure trends and insulin resistance levels, which are all part of Google's new AI-based Health Guardian suite.
Existing features like automatic workout detection are also being improved, and Google has also announced several partnerships with other health organizations to offer cross-platform compatibility with a variety of third-party services, devices, and apps. Some of these features are already rolling out, while users can expect others closer to the end of the month.
The American Heart Association labels hypertension (high blood pressure) as a 'silent killer' due to its lack of apparent symptoms until detected through screening. With nearly half of the adult population in the U.S. suffering from hypertension and being at risk of a heart attack or other health complications, monitoring blood pressure is extremely important — and Google is making it convenient for those with a Fitbit Air.
Google's new Health Guardian suite of features includes blood pressure trend tracking for users with a Google Health Premium subscription, which costs $9.99 monthly or $99.99 annually. This uses the watch's optical heart rate and motion sensors alongside Google's WavesFM AI model to passively measure your blood pressure trends throughout the day and warn you of any risks on the first of every month. Google states that this isn't meant to replace a dedicated blood pressure measuring device, but it provides a proactive way to notice changes without having to visit a doctor. It's also worth noting that neither the Fitbit Air nor Google Pixel watches support on-demand blood pressure readings.
Blood pressure monitoring is nothing new in the wearable space. The 2021 Huawei Watch D offered background blood pressure tracking and on-demand measurements using a mechanical pump built into the watch, and U.S. owners of select Samsung Galaxy watches, such as the Galaxy Watch 9 (with an external pump), and owners of Apple wearables like the Apple Watch Series 12 also got the feature earlier this year. Google Pixel watches and the Fitbit Air were a notable exception until now.
Another frequently undetected condition that can pose severe risks is insulin resistance or impaired insulin sensitivity. Insulin regulates blood sugar by aiding cells in the absorption of glucose to produce energy, and consistent resistance to it can lead to conditions like prediabetes and Type 2 diabetes, as well as other health complications.
Google is adding insulin resistance monitoring to the Fitbit Air with Health Guardian for users with Google Health Premium. This uses data gathered throughout the month from many of the sensors already in the Fitbit — optical heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and an accelerometer — and warns you of any detected trends that may present potential risks. Until now, only the Google Pixel Watch 5 had this feature, and now the Fitbit Air is also set to receive it. However, note that this feature only provides trend data and cannot provide on-demand insulin or blood glucose levels.
Beyond the newly added health metrics coming with Health Guardian, Google has also greatly improved certain existing features. If you've ever forgotten to start tracking a workout on your Pixel Watch or Fitbit Air, you might've noticed that it often intelligently does so without any manual input. The feature responsible for this is automatic activity detection, which is getting a huge upgrade in October.
Google states that automatic activity detection is going to be twice as accurate. This is possible using an AI model that will analyze context, such as your daily habits, when and how you work out, and manually added data. The number of supported workouts has also been expanded: the feature could initially detect only 10 activities, a number that has now been increased to over 100. The updated list of workouts includes swimming, strength training, certain racket and team sports, and more.
The Fitbit Air is a capable fitness band, but a standalone wrist-based tracker can only do so much by itself. You'll ultimately have to rely on other apps and equipment for specialized measurements, and managing different sources of data can be annoying. Fortunately, Google partners with several third-party health platforms and gives users the ability to sync and import data from a variety of apps and devices.
For instance, users with an Abbott Lingo continuous glucose monitor will soon be able to sync data with Google Health on select Google wearables, including the Fitbit Air. MyFitnessPal Premium users will now also be able to share food-specific logs with Google Health, and your Fitbit Air will get the ability to import lab results directly from Function Health later in the year. Starting early next year, users will also be able to sync Flo Health data with their Fitbit Air to receive more personalized advice from the Google Health Coach.

articles.title_orig: Supreme Court rejects alleged 9/11 mastermind’s attempt to revive plea deal
articles.title_zh: Supreme Court rejects alleged 9/11 mastermind’s attempt to revive plea deal
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal brought by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and two other alleged 9/11 plotters seeking to hold the government to a plea deal it later withdrew.
The court action removes one barrier to Mohammed standing trial before a military commission in 2028, where the death penalty is a possible punishment. He has been held at the U.S. base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, since 2006.
Mohammed is accused of being the ringleader of the plot to crash hijacked planes into the World Trade Center in New York and the Pentagon on Sept. 11, 2001. A fourth plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania.
The other two men who appealed to the Supreme Court were Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi and Walid bin Attash, who are also held at Guantanamo and set to face trial.
The three men had agreed to a plea deal with military prosecutors in 2024, signed off on by a military commission judge, that would have given them life sentences.
But days later, then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin rejected the proposal, saying he had the authority to override the deal.
Military courts said he had no such authority but, in an August ruling, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit ruled in favor of the government , prompting the men to appeal to the Supreme Court.
They argued, among other things, that the appeals court had no authority to intervene in the case.
The long delay in Mohammed facing trial was caused partly by concerns about evidence obtained via CIA torture.
A fourth alleged plotter earmarked for trial, Ali Abdul Aziz Ali, was not involved in the appeal.
Lawrence Hurley is a senior Supreme Court reporter for NBC News.

Long-haul flights can be as tiresome and boring as they are exciting. Spending hours on a flight and at airports requires preparation to ensure you not only have fun during travel but also arrive at your destination with your phones and other devices topped up. This includes creating the perfect flight kit with tech gadgets like a long-lasting, TSA-approved power bank , a good set of noise-canceling headphones , an international travel adapter, and even tracking tags for peace of mind about the security of your prized possessions during your trip.
Luckily, you can find all these essential travel gadgets in one place: Ugreen. The popular consumer electronics brand sells a wide variety of charging accessories, as well as audio equipment and location trackers. That said, because it has a large library of products, it can be slightly confusing to know which ones to pick before you catch your next flight.
But we're here to help you. We've used our experience testing and comparing tech accessories to identify the top five Ugreen gadgets worth adding to your long-haul flight kit. These include a 20,000 mAh fast-charging wired power bank , a 10,000 mAh wireless power bank, a pair of over-ear headphones, and Ugreen's AirTag-like tracker tags. Even better, they're all budget-friendly and easily available on Amazon.
The Ugreen Nexode 20,000 mAh power bank is an ideal option for long-haul flights, even those that include long layovers. Its massive battery capacity means you can charge your devices multiple times before the power bank itself needs a recharge. According to Ugreen itself, the power bank can top up the iPhone 16 Pro 3.7 times, the Galaxy S25 Ultra three times, and even heavier-duty tech gadgets like the iPad Pro and MacBook Air more than once. At the time of writing, this budget-friendly power bank is available on Amazon for just $59.99, with a very strong 4.4-star rating after more than 5,500 reviews.
Another big selling point of this Ugreen power bank is its charging speed. It can deliver power at 100 W through its main USB-C outlet, which can juice up nearly any phone from 0% to 50% in less than half an hour. It also comes with a USB-C cable capable of supporting 100 W fast charging, so you don't have to spend extra. It's also got two other outlets: another USB-C with a 30 W output and one USB-A port with 22.5 W max output. In total, you can simultaneously charge three devices. Just note that in that case, the main USB-C port caps out at 65 W, which is still plenty fast.
Users also like how lightweight and compact this power bank is. It measures 5.47 by 3.23 by 1.02 inches and weighs just 0.925 pounds. One reviewer said, "it fits comfortably in a backpack and will charge multiple devices quickly." Lastly, we also like that the power bank itself charges quickly. It can charge at 65 W, going from nil to full in around two hours, according to Ugreen.
Although Ugreen is popular for its battery packs, docks, chargers, and other related accessories, it's also got a healthy lineup of headphones and earbuds. And the Ugreen HiTune Max5c wireless over ear headphones are a particularly great gadget for frequent flyers , thanks mainly to their value for money. They're priced at just $35.99 on Amazon, where they enjoy a solid 4.4-star rating after more than 2,200 reviews. According to expert hands-on testing at Hi-Tech.UA , their "sound is exactly at the level of models twice as expensive," while one everyday reviewer said that they're "similar quality to headphones that cost over $200."
They rock a 40 mm dynamic driver and offer punchy bass and surprisingly crisp highs. They're also certified to support Hi-Res audio, thanks to LDAC decoding, which reduces audio loss and latency during wireless transmission. Moreover, these are also noise-canceling headphones. They feature adaptive ANC with multiple modes, including complete isolation — Ugreen says its AI noise-canceling chip can reduce 43 dB of noise — and a transparency mode, giving you greater control over your surroundings. They can both dampen and totally eliminate the chatter around you during flights.
They also provide a comfortable fit. They've got a thick headband, big ear cushions that are made of soft leather and are easy to rotate (90-degree internal rotation and 15-degree external rotation) and extend, and a metal frame that makes them flexible yet robust. Despite their voluminous appearance, though, they weigh just 0.58 pounds, making them easy to wear for long periods. One reviewer said, "I watched two movies on the plane back to back with no pain." Lastly, the battery life is also great, at 75 hours with ANC off and 45 hours with ANC on.
Ugreen's FineTrack Mini 2 are small tracking devices that let you monitor the live location of your precious belongings, whether it's the hand luggage you take with you in the airplane cabin or your suitcases that often become difficult to find in that crowded conveyor belt, as well as other things like your wallet and keys. A pack of four (iOS only) currently costs just $31.99 on Amazon, with a 4.4-star rating after over 500 reviews. Even better, your purchase includes a keychain attachment case for each of the four air trackers.
One of their biggest pros is that they're compatible with Apple's Find My app , so you don't have to install any third-party application. Moreover, setup is seamless and straightforward. All you have to do is open Find My and add it as an object. And if you're running iOS 17 or later, you also have the ability to share the tracker's location with others. In addition to a long battery life of 5-7 years, they're also built to be easily found in the dark, courtesy of their fluorescent design.
They have an IP68 rating, so they can withstand harsh outdoor conditions, including heavy rain. We also like their alert system, which sends notification to you in the event your item has moved a bit too far. There's also an alarm feature, which produces loud 110 dB sounds at the press of a button to help you locate the tracker when it's nearby. One reviewer remarked that they're even louder than Apple's AirTags and called them "hands down a better buy than AirTags." For context, a pack of four AirTags costs around $99 — about thrice the price of Ugreen's air trackers.
A wireless power bank is the perfect fit for when you want to charge your phone on the flight without having to clutter your tray space with wires. The Ugreen MagFlow 10,000 mAh Qi2 wireless power bank , then, is worth your attention. It's compatible with the latest Qi2.2 wireless charging standard and can therefore charge any iPhone from iPhone 16 onward at 25 W, which is the fastest possible wireless charging speed available in Western markets right now. That equals 0-50% on the iPhone 17 Pro Max in around 38 minutes. It can also charge an iPhone 12-15, albeit at 15 W.
Right now, it's available on Amazon for $64.99, with a 4.5-star rating after more than 2,200 reviews. It comes with 17 magnets for easy snaps and solid grip. One reviewer said, "The magnetic hold is excellent. It stays securely attached to the phone and does not slide around." It can also function as a typical wired power bank, as it has two USB-C outlets capable of delivering 30 W of power output. One of them is the integrated USB-C cable that also functions as a carrying strap.
The power bank recharges at 30 W, meaning it'll take around two hours for a full recharge. Users also like the little display it comes with. "[It] helps keep track of how much juice we have left to squeeze," as one Amazon reviewer put it. It also has light indicators to show when wireless and fast charging are on or off. Additionally, it's convenient to carry around with you on flights. That's because it weighs just 0.56 pounds and measures 4.36 by 2.72 by 0.83 inches.

articles.title_orig: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das To Remain In Jail, Custody Extended By 2 Days
articles.title_zh: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das To Remain In Jail, Custody Extended By 2 Days
articles.content_orig:
NEW DELHI, Oct 19 (Reuters) - An Indian court said on Monday two "Cockroach" movement leaders would stay in prison for two more days, local media reported, after they were ‌detained last week for demonstrating at a historic protest venue in violation of a ban.
Cockroach ‌Janta Party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were among 14 people who scaled barricades on Tuesday to enter the Jantar ​Mantar observatory, a day after it was removed from a list of designated protest sites.
They unfurled the Indian flag and chanted slogans demanding the chief election commissioner's resignation before police detained them, with a court later sending them to prison for five days.
On Monday evening, a local court extended their judicial custody ‌by two days after Delhi Police ⁠requested more time to question them, local media reported.
Delhi Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"This is an absolute mockery of the judicial ⁠system," the group's legal head, Ratna Singh, told reporters outside the court, adding they would challenge the order in a higher court.
The youth-led CJP, opposition parties and left-wing student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding ​Chief Election ​Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists ​that they say favours Prime Minister ‌Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders and several of their supporters were also detained on Friday as hundreds poured into central Delhi for a protest in support of Das and Ranka.
The 'Cockroach' movement has ‌emerged as one of the biggest political challenges to Modi ​and his BJP in his 12 years in power.
A weeks-long ​sit-in by the group and its supporters ​earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over ‌exam paper leaks.
The latest demonstrations erupted after the ​Indian Express newspaper reported ​that Kumar's two deputies had raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.
The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year — equivalent to ​more than the population of ‌Japan — included 28 million people who have died, 63 million who have relocated and 30 ​million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission.
(Reporting by Saurabh Sharma, ​writing by Sakshi Dayal; Editing by Hugh Lawson)

articles.title_orig: ‘Happy Birthday, Vlad. Yours, Always.’ - DJT.
articles.title_zh: ‘Happy Birthday, Vlad. Yours, Always.’ - DJT.
articles.content_orig:
In Donald Trump’s telling, he wins everywhere, from Florida to California, when the votes are counted properly, and his campaign rallies do nothing but juice the Republicans he deigns to share the stage with. “MY RALLIES ARE SAVING THE REPUBLICAN PARTY, AGAIN!!!” he wrote this month.
But Punchbowl News notes this morning that Trump’s actions tell a different story. Even though Trump said in September that he’d spend the last month before the midterms rallying the faithful in battleground districts, Trump has been steering well clear of competitive House races, preferring to play defense in parts of the country where voters are friendlier (and his crowds are larger).
This is worth remembering, ahead of whatever stolen-election nonsense Trump tries to pull next month: Deep down, even Trump knows he’s not as popular as he pretends to be. Happy Monday .
Join Will Sommer and Sam Stein today for MAGA Mondays at the early time of 9:00 a.m. EDT on Substack and YouTube .
Almost two weeks ago, on October 7, Donald Trump mentioned offhand that it was Vladimir Putin’s birthday and the two of them had a call set up. The call went ahead two days later, and Trump has been snuggling closer to Russia and taking a sledgehammer to Ukraine ever since.
You could tell the birthday chat was trouble from the jump. Russian media cheerfully reported on the “substance” and “warmth” of the phone call, with Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov reporting that “nobody wanted to hang up first.” The same day, Trump abruptly announced a dramatic swerve in his own energy policy: Far from increasing sanctions pressure on Russia, Trump now said the United States would waive sanctions in order to start buying diesel fuel from Russia directly.
One day later, on Saturday, October 10, Trump still had Putin’s assessment of Ukraine and Volodymyr Zelensky top of mind. “[Zelensky] wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel,” Trump told reporters . He even called for Zelensky to be removed from office: “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals, and for some reason never does.” (Maybe it has something to do with Russia demanding he give it huge chunks of Ukraine as the price of peace. Hard to say, really.) The same day, Trump officials threatened that America might stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine if attacks on Russian energy infrastructure continued.
The next day, Trump placed Zelensky in an even greater bind by unilaterally announcing an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine. Neither side had agreed to any such thing. (“They agreed,” Trump added the next day , “because I said they agreed.”) Thanks to Trump’s renewed enthusiasm for Putin’s lies about the war, this announcement created immediate and massive diplomatic asymmetries. Ukraine, desperate to get back in Trump’s good books, immediately began trying to honor the energy ceasefire; Russia, eager to capitalize, kept right on pounding Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
Zelensky’s unilateral honoring of the energy ceasefire did little to change Trump’s mood. Instead, the United States spent last week handicapping Ukraine’s war efforts in big and small ways. On Tuesday, October 13, Russian missiles pounded Kyiv without the usual advance warning provided by U.S. intelligence. That same night, Ukraine discovered that new restrictions had been placed on its Starlink satellite internet service—crucial infrastructure without which it could not pilot its drones. This service would later be partially, but not entirely, restored; subsequent reporting from Reuters said that the order to slow Ukraine’s satellite internet came directly from the White House, although Trump denied that he ordered it personally. (Subsequent reporting suggested Starlink owner Elon Musk was the one who first proposed the slowdown.)
On Friday, October 16, Trump gave Russia even more sanctions relief—preventing new sanctions on Russia and tariffs on buyers of Russian oil from going into effect, although he himself signed those sanctions into law just last month.
Over and over again since the birthday call, Trump has made his new position on the war clear: Nothing but incentives and wheedling praise for Russia, the war’s imperial aggressor, and nothing but threats and insults for Ukraine, the war’s blameless defender. And yesterday, he gave us his clearest explanation of his thinking yet.
“My decision on Russia is a very simple one,” Trump posted on Truth Social.
Why the kid gloves for Russia?
“I . . . don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” Trump said. After all, look how nicely Russia was behaving!
“Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way.”
And anyway, what was so great about Zelensky and Ukraine?
“[Zelensky] is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including in the United States,” Trump went on. “Farmers, ranchers, and businesses of all kinds are suffering greatly from this, but Russia is, nevertheless, sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World.” Zelensky, Trump added, “doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did. He could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now.”
It’s amazing how many of Trump’s psychological pathologies are here on display at once. There is, of course, his bewildering personal adulation of Putin himself, which makes it all too easy for the Russian dictator to feed him out-and-out lies about the state of the conflict and who is responsible. There’s his alpha-dog approach to geopolitics, which he believes shows great strength and in reality shows great weakness: The United States, Trump apparently believes, ought not lift a finger or offer a word of protest if the world’s other great powers decide to invade their neighbors. Instead, those great powers must be cherished and coddled, lest we “drive them away from the bargaining table” and they decide to intervene in our own imperial adventures.
Note how different this argument is from the old MAGA ones about how the whole conflict is an expensive boondoggle halfway around the world that we shouldn’t be involved with at all. Trump, fully in his own imperial era, has jettisoned such provincial “Donroe Doctrine” thinking. He just argues, openly and explicitly, that it’s better for the United States to be allied with Russia. All this is music to Putin’s ears: The Russian dictator, the Wall Street Journal reports , is now proposing a tripartite summit between the United States, Russia, and China to hash out the ultimate fate of Ukraine.
If you’re as sick as we are of our president sucking up to tyrants, ride with us.
There’s another psychological need on display here, too. Over the last month, Trump has deliberately been trying to shift Americans’ focus away from his interminable boondoggle in Iran and back toward the conflict in Ukraine.
Part of the idea is to get them to blame high gas prices not on Trump, who attacked Iran, but on Zelensky and/or Putin. But it’s also a matter of presidential posture. In Iran, Trump looks feckless and weak. He doesn’t have the stomach to escalate the war further, and Iran keeps flatly ignoring his threats to do so: Remember his July ultimatum that he would blow up “ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT” for every ship Iran attacked in the Strait of Hormuz?
In the Russia–Ukraine conflict, however, Trump thinks he looks strong. After all, Ukraine needs the United States—and how better to demonstrate that need than by withholding the things they need while lecturing them that it’s really their own fault? When the focus is on Iran, Trump looks like a wimp. When it’s on Ukraine, he thinks he looks cruel, but also strong. He knows which focus

articles.title_orig: Ukraine claims world’s first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
articles.title_zh: Ukraine claims world’s first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone.
The “historic” mission comes just as Kyiv faces a dire turn in its relationship with Washington over the withdrawal of support in its fight against Russia .
Shared by the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade on Monday, the video shows the soldier strapping himself into a large drone and being flown at what appears to be relatively low altitude over blurred-out territory. The drone carefully lowers him down and the drone operator greets him with “Welcome back to the ground!” The video also showed blurred faces of drone operators who carried out the mission.
The post said the unidentified infantryman was wounded while at his position. “Due to intense enemy drone activity and the presence of landmines, evacuation using conventional unmanned ground vehicles was impossible,” the brigade said.
“At that point, the specialists in our unit took it upon themselves to attempt something that had never been done before: evacuating a serviceman using an aerial drone,” it added.
The craft used was a heavy-lift hexacopter, it said, originally designed as a bomber by a Ukrainian manufacturer. It looks about twice the size of the soldier in the video.
The specialists working on the mission had to ensure the drone could carry a human being without flipping over or swaying excessively, according to the unit.
The rescued soldier is currently undergoing treatment and rehabilitation, the brigade added. The squad leader and programmer with the brigade, only identified by his call sign Napalm, called the soldier a “hero” for agreeing to the mission, “having seen and heard the kind of machine that had arrived to get him.”
In a separate statement, Ukraine’s Ground Forces said its drone units are already conducting operations “that were recently considered science fiction.”
The war has increasingly become a technological arms race, with both Ukraine and Russia relying on drones to reduce human casualties.
The conflict has taken a severe toll on both armies, although neither side reports up-to-date numbers of those killed, injured or missing. Ukraine in particular has faced a severe shortage of manpower as it has tried to ramp up recruitment.
Ukraine had a major leap in drone technology this year, allowing it to limit Russian logistics in occupied territories as well as strike deeper inside Russia to target Russian oil refineries , commercial warehouses and data centers .
“This mission proves once again that Ukrainian service members, working in tandem with Ukrainian manufacturers, are setting global trends in the conduct of warfare,” the brigade’s statement added.
Despite hoping that its drone innovation would give it the upper hand at the negotiating table, Kyiv has faced pressure from the U.S. to halt its strikes on Russian oil sites after President Donald Trump signed a diesel deal with the Kremlin earlier this month.
Kyiv has since also reported gaps in intelligence sharing and restrictions on Elon Musk’s Starlink service that is crucial for its drone missions, battlefield communications and air defense.
The drone evacuation comes just days after Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced the Ukrainian government had approved an “experimental project” to use drones for medical logistics. Koretskyi said flights would require coordination with the military, and drones would be given a special status and would be identifiable in the air.
“During the war, moving medical cargo by road can cost critical time, especially for transplants,” he said. “Drones will be able to carry medicines, medical products, blood samples, and donor organs between hospitals, including from remote areas.”
Yuliya Talmazan is a reporter for NBC News Digital, based in London.

articles.title_orig: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims
articles.title_zh: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims
articles.content_orig:
Uber has won its bid to throw out claims worth about £340m brought by thousands of London black cab drivers and two former private hire firms.
The claimants alleged the ride-hailing company gave Transport for London (TfL) misleading information when it first got a licence to operate in the capital in 2012.
But a High Court judge ruled the cases had been brought too late and dismissed them without considering whether the allegations were true.
Uber, which denied the claims, said it was pleased the court had thrown them out at the earliest opportunity.
About 13,000 drivers were seeking nearly £200m in damages, Reuters reported, while a claim on behalf of Kabbie and Iride, two private hire firms that have since closed, sought about £140m.
The lawsuits were filed in 2024, and Uber argued they fell outside the six-year limit for bringing such claims.
In a written ruling, Mr Justice Birt said the claimants could have discovered the alleged deception before 2018.
RGL Management, which ran the cases for the claimants, said it was very disappointed and was considering its options with the legal team.
Since gaining its licence, Uber has taken much of the trade once dominated by black cabs.
The company faces a separate case next week, when it challenges HM Revenue and Customs in a tax dispute worth more than £1bn.

articles.title_orig: Roche returns to China’s Hansoh for $15B biobucks ADC pact
articles.title_zh: Roche returns to China’s Hansoh for $15B biobucks ADC pact
articles.content_orig:
A year after their first antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) team-up, Roche has returned to Hansoh Pharmaceutical for a mammoth $15 billion biobucks pact.
The latest agreement spans a “broad portfolio of ADC programs,” Hansoh explained in an Oct. 19 release. They include two ADCs already in preclinical development at the Chinese biopharma, along with multiple programs focused on targets suggested by Roche but powered by Hansoh’s ADC tech.
The plan is for Jiangsu-based Hansoh to take these programs through phase 1 trials, before passing over responsibility to Roche to develop the ADCs worldwide—excluding Greater China.
In return, Hansoh will receive $400 million in upfront cash, followed by $110 million on the first anniversary of the deal. Further down the line, the biopharma is in line for potentially up to $15 billion in development, regulatory and commercialization milestones, as well as tiered royalties on sales if any ADCs make it to market.
The deal also has a clause where Hansoh could opt to contribute toward the global development of two programs from the collaboration. If it picks this route, Hansoh would become eligible to receive “incremental upside from the commercialization of these two programs,” according to the release.
This morning’s deal comes a year after Roche handed $80 million to Hansoh and pledged $1.45 billion in biobucks for the ex-China license to a CDH17-targeted ADC, dubbed HS-20110. At the time, HS-20110 was already in phase 1 testing in China and the U.S. as a potential treatment for colorectal cancer and other solid tumors.
“Building on the ADC partnership we announced last year, we are delighted to further strengthen our collaboration with Roche,” Eliza Sun, Executive Director of Hansoh’s board, said in this morning’s release.
“This new agreement reflects our shared commitment to advancing ADC innovation and underscores our strategy of leveraging our deep expertise to accelerate the development of transformative therapies for cancer patients globally,” Sun added.
Boris Zaïtra, head of corporate business development at Roche, said in this morning’s release that“expanding our strategic collaboration with Hansoh marks an important step in advancing our ADC vision.”
“Exploring next-generation ADCs is one of the most compelling frontiers in oncology today, offering the opportunity to address critical unmet needs and accelerate potential therapies for patients worldwide,” Zaïtra added.
Roche isn’t the only Big Pharma that’s turned to Hansoh to help power its ADC ambitions. GSK has already tasted clinical success with a pair of ADCs aimed at B7-H3 and B7-H4, respectively.
The B7-H3-directed ADC, dubbed ris-rez, recently achieved a median overall survival of 18.5 months in a phase 3 trial, lining up the therapy as a potential threat to Amgen and Merck & Co. in the lung cancer field. Last night, GSK unveiled the first global data for ris-rez, which demonstrated a 61% overall response rate in a phase 1b trial.
Jefferies analysts said that the readout helped move ris-rez from a therapy defined by its “impressive China phase 3” data to “a much more globally validated asset story.” Ris-rez is “starting to look like the B7-H3 ADC to beat in relapsed SCLC,” the analysts concluded.
Hong Kong-listed Hansoh has been one of the leading lights in China’s emergence as a biopharma innovation engine, notching collaborations with the likes of Merck & Co. and Regeneron . In August, Hansoh offered a bullish assessment of China’s innovative biopharma sector, arguing (PDF) that the industry is “fully transitioning from the ‘follower’ phase to the ‘frontrunner’ phase.”
This year, Hansoh stepped up spending to support its pipeline of more than 40 innovative medicine candidates that it is assessing in more than 70 clinical trials. R&D spending at the company jumped 20.7% to 1.7 billion Chinese yuan ($253 million) over the first half of the year.

articles.title_orig: US and China compete for influence in Central Asia
articles.title_zh: US and China compete for influence in Central Asia
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in Uzbekistan promoting trade and ties with Central Asia
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was in Uzbekistan on Monday to promote trade and ties with Central Asia, during a trip that came amid rumblings that America’s top diplomat is ignoring pressing matters in favor of politically safer visits and meetings.
The trip, which involves a stop in India later this week, seeks to promote U.S. economic and security ties with Central and South Asia . But it has only tangential links to the Trump administration’s current main foreign policy dilemmas in the Middle East and with the Russia-Ukraine war .
Rubio has brushed aside suggestions he is eschewing the most difficult issues in favor of taking on lower-hanging diplomatic fruit with less risk of failure and political damage, and the State Department pushed back on the criticism of his schedule.
In Samarkand, Rubio was meeting with his counterparts from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan under the C5+1 diplomatic forum, which brings together the five Central Asian countries and the United States to discuss security, trade and other shared concerns.
Speaking to reporters ahead of the meeting, Rubio said “the United States wants to be a strong partner in Central Asia.”
“Central Asia has just not gotten the level of attention from our policymakers over the last 20 years that it deserves. But that’s changing. That’s why we’re here now,” he said.
Despite repeated assurances from multiple administrations that the U.S. would become more actively involved in Central Asia, the region has often languished as a foreign policy priority in Washington.
After the collapse of the Soviet Union, the newly independent Central Asian nations saw a brief surge in U.S. interest, but that waned until after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks in the United States, which turned America’s attention once again toward Afghanistan and its neighbors.
The U.S. established a military presence in several countries mainly as transit points for equipment, materiel and provisions needed by U.S. and allied forces fighting the Taliban and al-Qaida in Afghanistan.
As the U.S. wound down its 20-year operation in Afghanistan, the Trump administration, in both its first and second terms, has sought to elevate its ties with Central Asia due to its location between Russia and China, but also as an underdeveloped area ripe for U.S. business opportunities.
Rubio’s trip, which has been heavily promoted by the U.S. ambassador to India and special presidential envoy for Central Asia, Sergio Gor, is perhaps the most ambitious U.S. attempt in decades to boost economic and commercial ties with the region. Speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Rubio described “an incredible delegation” with representatives of almost 300 American businesses joining.
“Historically, Central Asia has been the crossroads for trade between the West and the East. And today, as part of a broader renaissance and global engagement, it stands once again to play that vital role in transnational commerce," he told officials at the meeting.
The region is "a new location for investment, and it serves as a new location for export, a central terminal out of which materials that are vital for the future of all nations are being delivered,” he added.
President Donald Trump hosted their leaders at a White House summit last November, and announced more than $130 billion in commercial deals, including agreements for regional airlines to purchase Boeing aircraft.
The administration has also been keen to get the Muslim majority countries to join the Abraham Accords, which expanded the number of Arab states with diplomatic ties with Israel. Kazakhstan, which had already recognized Israel, is the only one of the five to sign the accords .
Associated Press writer Matthew Lee in Washington contributed to this report.
